daily.ideas: Market Strategy: 2QCY26 Strategy Wrap; Sector Update: Plantation; Company Update: KJTS

news.h: EPF becomes Eco-Shop's third-largest shareholder with 5.1% stake
news.body: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) has emerged as a substantial shareholder in Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd after raising its stake in the fixed-price retailer to above 5.0%. The pension fund bought an additional 8.68 million shares, or about 0.15% of the group's stake, raising its holding to 5.1%, or 296.2m shares, according to Eco-Shop's filing with Bursa Malaysia. This makes the EPF the third-largest shareholder in Eco-Shop, behind the founder and managing director who holds a 73.8% stake, and Agathis Montana Sdn Bhd, a vehicle managed by Creador IV, with a 7.5% stake.
takeaways: The incremental purchase was small — 8.68m shares, about 0.15% of the company — so this is a disclosure triggered by crossing the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold rather than a large new position being built in one go.

The ownership structure matters more than the stake itself: with the founder and managing director on 73.8% and Creador's Agathis Montana vehicle on 7.5%, roughly four-fifths of Eco-Shop already sits in two hands, so EPF's 5.1% is a minority position in a tightly held register.

Now that EPF is above the substantial-shareholder threshold, every subsequent move it makes must be disclosed, which gives the market continuing visibility into a domestic institution's view on the fixed-price retail format.
None of the three Kenanga reports in today's bundle covers Eco-Shop or fixed-price retail, so this is standalone digest context rather than a read-across to a covered name.

It does sit alongside today's Market Strategy note, which reports that consumer spending 'remains selective, with essentials resilient while discretionary demand, particularly apparel, remains soft' and where Kenanga trimmed target-price upside for some consumer names — a domestic institution adding to a value retailer is consistent with the essentials-resilient half of that split.

news.h: Central Global plans to raise up to RM83.0m via private placement for Sabah construction projects
news.body: Manufacturing and construction company Central Global Bhd is planning to raise up to RM83.3m through a private placement, mainly to fund its ongoing construction projects in Sabah. The group said it plans to issue up to 106.6m new shares, equivalent to 10.0% of its enlarged issued share capital (assuming the full exercise of its 51.8m outstanding Warrants B), to third-party investors at an issue price to be determined later. As at Aug 27, Central Global had an issued share capital of RM305.2m comprising 1.0b shares and 51.8m Warrants B.
takeaways: The digest's own headline gives the raise as 'up to RM83.0m' while its body text says 'up to RM83.3m'. The two differ by RM0.3m and Kenanga does not reconcile them, so both are reproduced here rather than one being silently chosen.
The issue price is explicitly 'to be determined later', which means any ringgit figure attached to this placement is an indicative maximum rather than a committed amount raised.

106.6m new shares against an existing 1.0b in issue is about 10% dilution of the enlarged base, and it is being placed with third-party investors rather than offered to existing holders — so current shareholders absorb the dilution without an entitlement.
Funding construction work in progress with fresh equity rather than borrowing against the order book points to working-capital pressure on the Sabah projects specifically.

Central Global is not covered in today's Kenanga bundle. Today's Market Strategy note is constructive on construction order books (it records SUNCON guiding FY26 job wins of RM7-9b, up from RM6b, and KERJAYA expecting more than RM3b, up from RM2b), so this reads as a small-cap funding story rather than a sector-wide signal.

news.h: Mulpha invests in Sun Hung Kai-linked investment fund
news.body: Mulpha International Bhd has invested USD7.0m (RM28.3m) in SHK Latitude Alpha Fund, a multi-manager hedge fund portfolio, as part of its efforts to enhance risk-adjusted investment returns. The subscription forms part of the group's broader investment portfolio and the deployment of a limited portion of surplus funds, said Mulpha in a bourse filing. Cayman Islands-based SHK Latitude was established as an investment fund in April 2021 and is a subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed Sun Hung Kai & Co Ltd.
takeaways: The USD7.0m / RM28.3m pairing implies a conversion rate of about 4.04, consistent with the USD/MYR rate of 4.0455 printed in the same digest — the figures are internally coherent.

Mulpha frames the subscription as deploying 'a limited portion of surplus funds' to enhance risk-adjusted returns, which makes this a treasury allocation rather than a strategic move into fund management.
A multi-manager hedge fund holding is a liquid, arm's-length financial asset, so it should not change the property and hospitality earnings base on which Mulpha is normally assessed.

The same digest lists Mulpha International among its oversold stocks, with a 14-day RSI of 29.25 at a last price of RM2.83 against a 30-day low of RM2.82 — the company is deploying surplus cash while its own shares sit at the bottom of their recent range.
Mulpha is not covered in today's Kenanga bundle and no research view accompanies the item, so this is digest context only.

news.h: Kenanga's Islamic fund emerges as substantial shareholder in Sern Kou with 11.2% stake
news.body: One of the unit trust funds managed by Kenanga Investors Bhd has emerged as a substantial shareholder in furniture maker Sern Kou Resources Bhd. RHB Trustees Bhd, on behalf of Kenanga Islamic Absolute Return Fund, acquired 120.4m shares that represent an 11.2% stake in Sern Kou last Friday (Aug 28), according to Sern Kou's bourse filing. 'Kenanga Investor Bhd — the investment manager of Kenanga Islamic Absolute Return Fund — acquired the shares as part of portfolio investment,' the filing stated. The value of the transaction was not disclosed, and neither were details of the seller.
takeaways: Read the related-party angle first: this digest is published by Kenanga Investment Bank's research arm, and the buyer is a unit trust fund managed by Kenanga Investors Bhd, the asset-management arm. The filing describes the purchase as 'part of portfolio investment', not as a research recommendation.

Acquiring 11.2% — 120.4m shares — in a single dealing is a block trade rather than gradual accumulation, so the stake almost certainly came from an identified counterparty rather than the open market.

Neither the transaction value nor the seller was disclosed, so no price, premium or discount can be attached to the deal. Any implied valuation would have to be invented and is therefore not stated here.
The trade was executed on Friday 28 August and appears in this 3 September digest, which is a normal substantial-shareholder notification lag rather than a delayed disclosure.
Sern Kou is not covered in today's Kenanga bundle and carries no rating or target price from Kenanga research, so there is no house view to read alongside the stake.

news.h: Zecon proposes to sublease land for RM54.4m in related party deal
news.body: Zecon Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Zecon Renewables (Sarawak) Sdn Bhd (ZRSSB) has proposed subleasing a portion of land in Kuching, Sarawak, from Zecon Solar Sdn Bhd (ZSSB) in a related party transaction for RM54.4m. Zecon said the proposal entails subleasing 122.18 hectares (302 acres) for 30 years at a monthly rental rate of RM500 per acre. This translates to RM151,000 a month, and RM1.8m annually. The land forms part of the Kota Petra Green Technology Park in Kuching. It has been approved for a 100-megawatt alternating current (MWac) solar photovoltaic farm development.
takeaways: The filing's own arithmetic reconciles: 302 acres at RM500 per acre per month is RM151,000 a month and about RM1.8m a year, and RM1.8m across 30 years is roughly RM54.4m — so the headline RM54.4m is the undiscounted total rental commitment over the full term, not an upfront payment.

This is a related-party transaction between two Zecon entities, so the rental terms are not arm's-length by construction and will need the usual independent-adviser and shareholder scrutiny before completion.

The land is already approved for a 100 MWac solar photovoltaic farm within the Kota Petra Green Technology Park, so the sublease secures site tenure for a specific permitted project rather than for speculative landbanking.

Matching a 30-year land tenure to a long-dated renewable concession is the same structural logic behind the KJTS agreements in today's bundle, where 20-year operations-and-maintenance and chilled-water contracts run from March 2027 to February 2047 — in both cases the contract tenure is the asset.

Zecon is not covered in today's Kenanga bundle. The renewable-energy read-across in today's reports runs instead through SAMAIDEN and KJTS, which the Market Strategy note lists as its sector top picks for renewable energy and energy efficiency.

macro.h: US-Iran strikes raise fears of renewed war across the Middle East
macro.body: Fears of renewed escalation gripped the Middle East on Wednesday after the United States and Iran exchanged their biggest barrage since July, with Washington striking Iran's southern coast and Tehran firing at US bases across the region. (Reuters)
takeaways: The digest describes this as the biggest exchange since July, so it is an escalation of an existing conflict rather than the opening of a new one — the market has been pricing Middle East risk for months.
Nymex crude in the same digest is at USD91.0 a barrel, up 0.88% on the day, so the immediate oil-price reaction printed here is modest relative to the headline.

Today's Plantation sector note ties the conflict directly to palm oil economics: it cites higher biodiesel demand from the ongoing Middle East conflict, alongside Black Sea shipping disruption, as a reason to keep elevated CPO price assumptions of RM4,500 per tonne for CY26 and RM4,700 for CY27.

Today's Market Strategy note flags the same conflict as a cost-inflation channel, naming it as a key swing factor for technology firms and as the driver of an earlier cost spike for consumer names that has since stabilised.

The Malaysian fuel-price item elsewhere in today's macro bits notes prices rose towards the end of the pricing period 'amid heightened geopolitical tensions in West Asia', so the escalation is already feeding into the next domestic pricing cycle rather than the one just announced.

macro.h: Bessent urges BOJ chief to combat weak yen with 'decisive' monetary steps
macro.body: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent voiced strong support for 'decisive' monetary steps to combat yen weakness in a meeting with Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda, cementing the case for a Japanese rate hike this month. (Reuters)
takeaways: This is the second consecutive Bessent intervention on the yen recorded in Kenanga's digests — the 1 September edition carried him saying he expected Japan to act — so the pressure is sustained rather than a one-off remark.
The digest prints USD/YEN at 159.89, down 0.12% on the day from 160.09, so the yen is firming only marginally despite the rhetoric.

Nikkei 225 fell 2.85% to 64,325.6 in the same session, the largest single-day decline among the indices printed in today's digest — a rate-hike expectation is not a benign signal for Japanese equities.
A US Treasury Secretary publicly directing another country's central bank is itself the notable part: it converts a monetary decision into a bilateral trade-and-currency issue.
None of the three Kenanga reports in today's bundle carries direct Japan revenue exposure, so this is background macro context for Malaysian readers rather than a read-across to a covered row.

macro.h: Unsubsidised RON97, RON95 and diesel prices drop by five sen per litre from Sept 3
macro.body: The ministry said the lower prices reflected softer global crude oil prices for most of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) pricing period, although prices rose towards the end of the period amid heightened geopolitical tensions in West Asia. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The cut takes effect on 3 September, the date of this digest, so it is a live change to domestic pump prices rather than a proposal.

The ministry's own explanation contains the caveat that matters: the five-sen cut reflects softer crude for most of the pricing period, but prices rose towards the end of it — so the next APM cycle starts from a higher base if West Asian tensions persist.
Five sen a litre is a small move against the Nymex crude price of USD91.0 a barrel printed in the same digest; the Automatic Pricing Mechanism smooths rather than transmits crude volatility.
This is the unsubsidised price for all three grades, so the direct beneficiaries are commercial and non-subsidised users rather than Budi95-eligible motorists.

Today's Market Strategy note records that ports and logistics players have been managing unsubsidised diesel costs — it cites an extra RM50m cost for WPRTS to be handled through cost pass-through, electrification and solar-powered cranes and trucks — so a five-sen reduction is a marginal easing of a cost line those operators are already engineering around.

macro.h: Food prices push inflation higher, BI set to hold
macro.body: Indonesia's headline inflation rose to 3.19% YoY in August (Jul: 2.88%), slightly above consensus (3.13%) but stayed within Bank Indonesia's (BI) 1.5% - 3.5% target range for a sixth straight month. 2026 inflation outlook held at 3.1% (2025: 1.9%), with upside risk that could lift inflation to 3.3%. (See Economic Viewpoint: Indonesia Consumer Price Index)
takeaways: At 3.19% the August print is above consensus of 3.13% but still inside BI's 1.5%-3.5% target band for a sixth consecutive month, so it is a beat on the number without being a breach of the target.

Kenanga holds its 2026 Indonesia inflation outlook at 3.1% against 1.9% in 2025, and explicitly names an upside risk that could take it to 3.3% — the forecast is unchanged but the risk is stated as skewed one way.
Food prices are identified as the driver, which is the least policy-responsive component and therefore the weakest case for BI to tighten in response.

The reference in this bullet points to Kenanga's separate Economic Viewpoint on the Indonesia CPI, which was published in the 2 September bundle and is not part of today's three-report line-up, so the underlying note is not one of today's rows.
The JCI closed at 6,595.8, down 0.06%, in the same session — the inflation surprise produced no meaningful equity-market reaction.

macro.h: BOJ's Takata urges nimble rate hikes, says 2026 marks a turning point
macro.body: The Bank of Japan should conduct interest rate hikes nimbly to counter intensifying inflationary pressures, rather than adhere to a fixed semiannual pace anticipated by markets, hawkish board member Hajime Takata said on Wednesday. (Reuters)
takeaways: Takata's argument is about the pace and predictability of tightening, not its direction: he is arguing against the fixed semiannual cadence the market has assumed, which implies more frequent moves than currently priced.
The digest labels Takata a hawkish board member, so this is a directional voice within the committee rather than the BOJ's settled position.
It lands alongside the Bessent item in the same macro section, meaning both external pressure and internal hawkishness are pointing the BOJ the same way in the same digest.
The Nikkei's 2.85% fall to 64,325.6 in this session is consistent with a market repricing the near-term rate path, though the digest does not attribute the move to any single cause.
For Malaysian readers the transmission is via the yen and regional risk appetite rather than earnings; none of today's three Kenanga reports carries Japan exposure.

macro.h: RBNZ delivers back-to-back rate hikes to curb inflation
macro.body: New Zealand's central bank is raising its key interest rate for a second straight meeting, aiming to shift to less stimulatory settings in an effort to head off inflationary pressures. (The Star)
takeaways: A second consecutive hike establishes a tightening sequence rather than a one-off adjustment, and the stated aim is to move to 'less stimulatory' settings rather than to restrictive ones.
The RBNZ is acting pre-emptively — the digest frames the move as heading off inflationary pressures rather than responding to an overshoot already recorded.

Together with the BOJ, ECB and Bank of Canada items in the same macro section, today's digest carries four separate central banks either hiking or signalling hikes — the global direction of travel in this edition is uniformly tighter.

That global tightening backdrop is relevant to the MGS argument in today's Market Strategy note, which warns that US inflation concerns have spiked treasury yields, that this feeds local MGS yields, and that higher MGS rates weigh on banks' markets income.
New Zealand has no direct read-across to any of today's three Kenanga reports; the value of the item is as one more data point in the tightening cycle.

macro.h: US private payroll growth slows in August; factory orders rebound in July
macro.body: US private payrolls increased less than expected in August as strength in the education and health services sector was offset by job losses in manufacturing and a few other industries. (Reuters)
takeaways: The composition is the story: education and health services gains were offset by manufacturing job losses, so the labour market is not weakening uniformly but rotating away from goods production.
The headline pairs a weaker August labour print with a July factory-orders rebound, which are different months — the labour data is the more current signal of the two.
A softer private payrolls number cuts against the hawkish tone running through the rest of today's macro bits, so the US data is not pointing in one clean direction.

US equities nonetheless rose in the session printed in this digest — Dow Jones +0.56%, S&P 500 +0.46%, NASDAQ +0.45% — consistent with slower payrolls being read as reducing rather than raising rate pressure.
For Malaysia the channel is the dollar and treasury yields rather than trade volumes; USD/MYR at 4.0455 was 0.16% weaker for the ringgit on the day.

macro.h: Fed's Beige Book shows economic activity up modestly
macro.body: US economic activity increased modestly in the past two months with demand from data centers driving growth. The outlook for the economy was 'positive,' though sentiment was mixed across sectors amid uncertainty about energy prices and geopolitics. (Bloomberg)
takeaways: Data centre demand is named as the growth driver in the Fed's own survey, which is the same theme today's Market Strategy note identifies as the only source of meaningful valuation multiple expansion in Malaysia in August.
The Beige Book describes activity as up 'modestly' with mixed sectoral sentiment, which is a description of uneven rather than broad growth.
Uncertainty about energy prices and geopolitics is cited directly by the Fed's contacts, linking this item to the US-Iran escalation at the top of today's macro section.
The Beige Book is qualitative survey evidence, not data — it should be read alongside the softer August private payrolls print in the same digest rather than instead of it.

Today's Malaysian read-across is thematic: the Market Strategy note attributes August's 7% construction and 8% utilities index gains to hyperscaler data centre EPCC awards and YTLPOWR's expanded colocation ambitions, the same demand source the Fed is describing.

macro.h: Trump pledged fiscal restraint. Instead, debt tops USD40t as borrowing costs rise
macro.body: Donald Trump returned to the White House promising to get the United States' financial house in order by slashing the scope of the federal government, ending costly 'forever wars' and spurring economic growth to tame spiraling deficits. (Reuters)
takeaways: The USD40t threshold is the reportable fact here; the digest gives no deficit or issuance figures alongside it, so the debt level is stated without a flow number to explain it.
The item pairs a rising debt stock with rising borrowing costs, which is the combination that matters for treasury yields rather than either fact alone.

Today's Market Strategy note makes the Malaysian consequence explicit: concerns over US inflation have spiked the US treasury market, which influences local MGS yields, which in turn hits fair valuations of banks' investment bond securities.

That same note argues a markets-income recovery for Malaysian banks in 3Q26 would be 'a tall order' given MGS rates that have crept up continually through the quarter — this item is the upstream cause of that view.
This bullet is a narrative piece rather than a data release, so it should be treated as context on the direction of US fiscal risk rather than as a dated data point.

macro.h: Bank of Canada holds key rate, says multiple hikes might be needed
macro.body: The Bank of Canada kept its key policy rate on hold at 2.25% on Wednesday, as widely expected, but Governor Tiff Macklem said policymakers were prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high. (Reuters)
takeaways: The decision was a hold at 2.25% and was widely expected, so the market-relevant content is entirely in the guidance rather than the rate itself.
Macklem's reference to multiple hikes is explicitly conditional on inflation remaining too high — it is a stated reaction function, not a committed path.
Canada's 2.25% policy rate sits below Malaysia's 2.75% OPR, which Kenanga has expected BNM to hold through 2026 in its recent economic viewpoints.
This is the fourth central bank in today's macro section leaning hawkish, after the BOJ, RBNZ and ECB items, reinforcing the tightening-bias backdrop.
There is no direct link to any of today's three Kenanga reports; the relevance is to the global rate backdrop behind the MGS-yield argument in today's Market Strategy note.

macro.h: Nagel signals ECB will hike next week, cautious beyond that
macro.body: Governing Council member Joachim Nagel indicated that the European Central Bank will raise borrowing costs next week, though he stayed wary of what comes after that. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Nagel signals a near-certain hike at next week's meeting but explicitly withholds guidance beyond it — the signal is about one meeting, not a cycle.
This is a single Governing Council member speaking, so it indicates the likely decision rather than confirming it.
EUR/USD in the same digest is at 1.1572, weaker by 0.17% on the day, so the expected hike is not currently supporting the euro.

It adds the ECB to the BOJ, RBNZ and Bank of Canada in today's macro section as central banks tightening or signalling tightening, against a Fed that today's US payrolls print made marginally less hawkish.
Malaysia's exposure here is indirect — via global rates and the ringgit — and none of today's three Kenanga reports carries direct eurozone revenue exposure.

macro.h: Banks rush to swap higher-risk credit assets for Bank of England cash
macro.body: British banks are increasingly pledging higher-risk assets such as loans linked to high-interest store cards and vehicle leases as collateral at the Bank of England. (Reuters)
takeaways: The signal is in the collateral mix, not the volume: store-card and vehicle-lease loans are being pledged, which are among the higher-risk categories a central bank will accept.
Banks reaching further down the collateral stack to obtain central bank cash is conventionally read as a funding-conditions indicator rather than a lending-demand one.
The digest gives no amounts, no time series and no named institutions, so the trend is directional only and no magnitude can be attached to it.
This is a UK-specific funding story with no stated read-across to Malaysian banks; the FTSE-100 fell 0.30% in the same session.

Today's Market Strategy note discusses Malaysian bank balance sheets through a different channel entirely — MGS yields and investment-securities valuations, not collateral quality — so the two should not be conflated.

reports.flag: The Kenanga Signal on this row reads None stated because KJTS's own Company Update contains no pick declaration — only an 'Investment thesis' paragraph beginning 'We like KJTS for...'. Kenanga's separate Market Strategy note in the same 3 September bundle does list KJTS (with SAMAIDEN) under 'Sector Top picks' for Renewable Energy & Energy Efficiency (Exhibit 11). That statement sits in a different report and is recorded on the Market Strategy row, not inferred onto this one.
reports.name: KJTS Group Berhad
reports.catalyst: Maintained OUTPERFORM; TP raised c.2% to RM1.60 (from RM1.57) after Thai subsidiary KJTN Engineering signed four 20-year retrofit, O&M and chilled-water agreements with Central Plaza Hotel (Centel) subsidiaries, lifting FY26F/FY27F earnings by 2% and 5%.
reports.quote: We are positive on the agreements, as they further strengthen KJTS's recurring income base with a 20-year tenure, while expanding its energy services footprint in Thailand.
summary: The four agreements cover retrofit works, O&M services and chilled-water supply at four Centel hotels — Centara Reserve Samui, Centara Hotel Hat Yai, Centara Grand Beach Resort Phuket and Centara Karon Resort Phuket — with total retrofit capex of c.RM11m (RM11.2m in Exhibit 1) and total fixed fees of c.RM48m (RM47.8m) over 20 years, or c.RM2.4m of annual recurring revenue, plus monthly variable fees based on chilled water supplied.

The near-term earnings effect is small and the timing is the reason: retrofit works complete by February 2027 and the 20-year O&M and chilled-water period only runs from March 2027 to February 2047, so Kenanga raises FY26F earnings by just 2% and FY27F by 5%, with a full-year contribution expected only from FY27 once all four systems are operational.

The target price rises to RM1.60 from RM1.57 on a DCF-based sum-of-parts. Within that SoP the Thailand energy-efficiency projects (49% stake) are carried at RM17.7m against a total equity value of RM1,124.0m, so the four hotels move the valuation only marginally; the EPCC segment at 16x FY27F PER (RM440.3m) and Stonepeak's potential at RM0.80 a share remain the dominant components.

On funding, Kenanga assumes an 80:20 debt-to-equity structure and variable fees of 0.14 sen/RTh to estimate a high-single-digit IRR, and notes gross gearing of 0.23x as at 30 June 2026 with no major hurdles foreseen in securing project financing — the RM11m capex is ultimately funded by KJTS.

Kenanga's stated conviction language here is limited to an investment-thesis line ('We like KJTS for' Malaysia's RM41b energy-efficiency opportunity, the underappreciated 10% Stonepeak JV, and MUSB), which is not a pick declaration — so this row reads None stated on the strict rule. Kenanga's separate Market Strategy report in the same bundle does name KJTS a sector top pick for Renewable Energy & Energy Efficiency; that is recorded on the Market Strategy row. Risks Kenanga names are Stonepeak JV termination or delay, a rollback of the government's energy-efficiency policy, and concession asset termination.

analyst.note: The most recent publicly retrievable named-house call on KJTS is CIMB Securities on 13 Mar 2026, after the FY25 results briefing: "With no surprises from KJTS’ FY25 results briefing, we make no changes to our FY26 to FY28 earnings per share (EPS) estimates, ‘buy’ rating and target price of RM1.10 a share". Read the date — this call is nearly six months older than the Kenanga note beside it and predates both the iHandal acquisition being fully reflected and the four Thai Centel agreements announced on 2 Sep 2026, so CIMB’s RM1.10 is stale rather than a live disagreement. CIMB used no pick language, so this row reads None stated. Buy versus Kenanga’s Outperform is the same direction, so no divergence flag is set. Of the nine houses searched, only CIMB Securities yielded a dated, publicly retrievable call on KJTS.
cites: The Star, 13 Mar 2026 — ‘KJTS eyes stronger earnings this year’
The Star, 2 Sep 2026 — ‘KJTS Thai unit secures 20-year hotel O&M, chilled water deals worth RM47.83mil’

Those figures are as quoted in this sector piece and have not been independently verified against stock-specific reports today.

reports.name: Plantation Sector Update: Impairment Mars 2Q Profit Uptick
reports.catalyst: Maintains OVERWEIGHT on Plantation with CPO price assumptions unchanged at RM4,500/MT for CY26 and RM4,700 for CY27; IOICORP (OP; TP RM5.40) remains the sector pick, HSPLANT (OP; TP RM3.00) is added as the smaller-cap pick, and KLK (OP; TP RM25.80) is held out as the CPO-price-sensitive large cap.
reports.quote: While its share prices have risen of late, IOICORP (OP; TP:RM5.40) remains our sector pick because of strong earnings outlook and its superior ROE still suggest good value.
summary: Sector 2QCY26 earnings were dragged down by a single non-plantation item: KLK impaired 90% of the carrying cost of its 27% stake in UK-listed Synthomer by RM1.625b, which more than offset SDG's RM443m land disposal gain and pushed sectorial non-plantation to a RM1.283b loss, against a RM160m profit in 1QCY26. Adjusted for one-offs, plantation earnings converged towards Kenanga and consensus expectations.

The results spread improved materially against Kenanga's own forecasts: 22% above, 44% within and 33% below in 2QCY26, versus 1QCY26 when nothing at all beat Kenanga's estimates (0% above, 56% within, 44% below). Against consensus the 2QCY26 split was roughly a third each.

Upstream earnings rose 27% QoQ and 3% YoY on better harvest (+14% QoQ, +1% YoY) and firmer prices (CPO +4% QoQ, +1% YoY; PK +10% QoQ, +4% YoY, which helped temper estimated cost inflation of around 5%). Adjusted upstream margin of 29% was up from 28% in 1QCY26 but a touch below 2Q25's 30%, and sits in the upper half of the past five-year range of 14-40%.

Downstream adjusted profit soared 123% QoQ and 264% YoY on firmer petrochemical prices, higher plant utilisation from restocking and fortuitous trading of cheaply secured inputs — Kenanga calls it the most profitable downstream quarter in three years. It expects that to fade: regional overcapacity should pull 2HCY26 and CY27 margins back to 2-3%, against 6% in 2QCY26.

OVERWEIGHT is maintained with CPO assumptions unchanged at RM4,500/MT for CY26 and RM4,700 for CY27, on El Nino (historically cutting palm oil output 2-9% and lifting CPO prices 5-10%), Middle East-driven biodiesel demand and Black Sea sunflower disruption; CPO has already risen 7% from a 1HCY26 average of RM4,329 to RM4,612 in August. Sector valuations of 14-16x PER and 1.3x PBV are described as undemanding, and sector net gearing was broadly flat at 34% against 33% a year ago.

reports.name: 2QCY26 Report Card: Rotating Within Sectors
reports.catalyst: FBM KLCI year-end target nudged up to 1,775 (from 1,770) on blended 2026/2027 EPS at 16x against a current 1,708; sector weights unchanged, but picks are switched within sectors — MAYBANK and HLBANK in for CIMB and PBBANK, QL in for MRDIY, SIMEPROP in for SPSETIA, and DIALOG preferred in oil and gas.
reports.quote: We deem the 2Q26 performance for the FBM KLCI as within historical norms and satisfactory against the backdrop of the Iran conflict.
summary: The FBM KLCI year-end target is raised only marginally to 1,775 from 1,770, on a top-down blended 2026/2027 EPS at 16x, and Kenanga expects the upcoming Budget and market reforms to provide the uplift. Post-2Q26 it now expects KLCI earnings growth of 6.8% (excluding PCHEM, which made a loss last year), against roughly 4% in its earlier strategy note, with the increase attributed chiefly to earnings upgrades at MISC and PMETAL.

2QCY26 was the cleanest results season of the five quarters tabulated: 21% of KLCI components beat, 66% were in line and 14% missed, with the broader coverage universe at 20% beat, 58% in line and 21% miss — the lowest miss rate in the table. Kenanga credits the technology sector for behaving better, names oil and gas as the worst offender, and reports the upgrade-to-downgrade ratio rising from 0.8x (9 up, 11 down) to 1.0x (5 up, 5 down).

The market punished misses more than it rewarded beats this quarter — Kenanga finds a results miss more likely to produce a negative share-price reaction than a beat is to produce a positive one across consumer, oil and gas and technology, with glovemakers falling despite beats on weaker ASP guidance, and energy the exception where misses did not correlate with negative prices.

Only construction, utilities and energy saw valuation multiple expansion in August. Construction and utilities indices rose 7% and 8% respectively on hyperscaler data centre EPCC awards and YTLPOWR's expanded colocation ambitions (TP raised to RM6.40 on a pipeline of more than 1.1 GW), with multiple expansion rather than earnings upgrades explaining most of the move.

Dividends and value unlocking are named as the sustaining themes. Kenanga believes the street still underappreciates ABMB (OP; TP RM5.50) for its dividend ability given excess capital, and has pencilled in an 8 sen special dividend from BURSA (OP; TP RM9.60) — its DPS expectations for ABMB, BURSA and SIMEPROP are all ahead of the street, while it has not yet done the same for RHBBANK (MP; TP RM8.40), whose management will elaborate on its capital-management framework in 1Q27. On the cautious side it stays contrarian on SUNMED (UP; TP RM1.75), deeming valuations rich after they exceeded those of Indian hospitals.
